title: "This app stopped my revenge trade"

"And no, it's not a broker setting. It's my journal."
Not my broker. My journal.
FACE: you at the desk, looking into the camera, half-smile.
"Two losses in a row. Heart racing. You open a bigger trade to win it back. You know this feeling."
2 losses… 😤
DESK: hand hovering over the mouse, chart full of red, close-up of your eyes.
"But here's what nobody tells you…"
Nobody tells you this 👇
TEXT CARD: black screen, white text, a short "boom" sound.
"Revenge trades have nothing to do with the market. They happen when emotions are running your account."
Emotions ≠ strategy

FACE: point down at the comments. End card: journzey · coming soon.

I'm building journzey to enforce it automatically. Coming soon 🔔

Even 60% win rate won't save you

title: "Same lot size, 5× the risk"
why: A surprising fact plus maths people save. Beginners share it with friends. Works without showing much of the app.
rows: "You're probably risking way more than you think."
You're risking MORE than you think
FACE: direct, serious.
"Because 0.5 lots on gold is NOT the same as 0.5 lots on EURUSD."
0.5 gold ≠ 0.5 EURUSD
TEXT: two lot tickets side by side.
"Gold: 0.5 lots with a $10 stop risks $500. EURUSD: 0.5 lots with a 20-pip stop risks $100."
Gold: $500 · EURUSD: $100
TEXT: two numbers counting up.
"Same lot size…"
Same lot size…
TEXT CARD.
"…five times the risk. That's how one gold trade wipes a week of forex profits."
5× the risk 😳
DESK: chart of gold moving fast.
"Fix: lots = (account × risk %) ÷ (stop distance × value per point). $10,000 at 1% with a $10 gold stop = 0.10 lots."
TEXT: the formula building step by step.
"journzey's risk calculator does this for every instrument in one second, from your own account size."
journzey · risk calculator
SCREEN: calculator, typing stop distance, lot size appearing.
"Save this before your next trade. Follow for launch."
Save before your next trade 🔖
FACE + end card.
caption:
0.5 lots on gold ≠ 0.5 lots on EURUSD 😳

Gold, $10 stop → $500 risk
EURUSD, 20-pip stop → $100 risk

Lot size should come from your stop, not your mood:
lots = (account × risk%) ÷ (stop × value per point)

title: "Moving your stop loss has a price"
feature: Edge Matrix: last-month audit ("Keep doing" / "Cut out")
why: A confession question ("YES or NO") gets very easy comments. The R maths is saveable value.
rows: "Moving your stop loss is costing you more than bad entries."
Moving your stop = 💸
SCREEN: dragging a stop loss further away on a chart.
"My journal put an exact price on it."
It put a PRICE on it
SCREEN: Edge Matrix "Cut out: Moving stop loss" chip (your number, or the demo labelled "sample data").
"You move it 'just a bit'. Sometimes price comes back. When it doesn't, a 1R loss becomes 2R or 3R."
DESK: frustrated hand off the mouse.
"Here's the maths that changed my mind."
The maths 👇
TEXT CARD.
"Win half your trades at 2R and lose 1R: you make half an R per trade. Let your losses grow to 2R and you make zero."
TEXT: two equity lines, one rising, one flat.
"Rule: a stop can only move toward profit, never away. Ever."
Stops move ONE way ➡️
TEXT + FACE.
"journzey's monthly audit shows what to keep doing and what to cut out, with the exact amount each habit cost you."
journzey · monthly audit
SCREEN: Last month audit, Keep doing / Cut out rows.
"Be honest: do you move your stop? Comment YES or NO."
YES or NO? 👇
FACE + end card.
caption:
Moving your stop "just a bit" has a price 💸

Win 50% at 2R, lose 1R → +0.5R per trade
Let losses grow to 2R → 0R

Rule: stops only move toward profit. Never away.

journzey shows exactly what each habit costs you. Coming soon 🔔
